It is cheaper to buy this game than just the emoticon on the market so here I am. I had no idea what to expect. 

It is modern arcade like. Reminds me of the N64 Alien game 👾 Space Invaders. It was fun for about 30 minutes and then I went a little cross-eyed when I realized I was going to have to keep playing for another hour and a half. 

There are various game modes giving you an array of gameplay styles to best suit you. In several modes you can select the map much like mario kart so the scenery and music changes. Selecting your skin and weapon is easy enough 😅

It's not bad but you won't see me playing 2,000 hours on this. This game is good for beginners learning WASD and perhaps those who never got to play the OG variations. 

I could have gotten more achievements in the 2 hours if I had researched prior but this will be a game you really have to enjoy/invest hours into to perfect the game to 100% completion. 

There is a pink foil alien badge for any girls who like the pink/spooky ones and of course the stars emoticon is used in multiple art creations for comments. I will paste my two favorites in the comments and you can decide if it's worth it to you ♥︎

That said, the game does offer co-op, so it might shine more as a couch co-op experience. Who knows—maybe that’s where it truly works best.

A game I can recommend to people that like shoot em ups but aren't very good at them.

There's many difficulty presets, the easiest one basically turns the game into a party game (which is just appropriate since it supports up to 4 players), the normal one should be just right for people vaguely familiar with the genre to beat, and everything after that provides more challenge to the more experienced players by altering many different aspects, not just enemy/bullet counts. There's even a custom preset where you can adjust all of these individual aspects to your liking to create your own experience.

Instead of ships, you have 5 mechs to choose from. After you choose a mech, you then choose a primary and secondary weapons. Each mech has access to the same arsenal, however, they also have two unique skills that significantly alter how they play. 

There's no one hit deaths, you got a life bar and a shield, the life bar requires a health pickup to refill but your shield regenerates after a few seconds of not taking damage. A very generous system, that said, there's no invincibility period or anything after getting hit, so going face-first into a thick bullet barrage will still kill you very fast.

Stages are split into 3 parts, each one serves as a checkpoint. Reaching the first two gives you a free upgrade to choose from 3 random choices, clearing the level allows you to use earned money to buy more upgrades from an also random but bigger selection, some of these upgrades are exclusive to the shop itself.

The whole campaign can be beaten in around 2 hours, give or take depending on difficulty and how often you die. The game does save your progress so you can beat it at your own leisure.

There's a few additional modes, but they're more like cool extras than anything you'll be spending a serious amount of time in, I see more replay value in the campaign and trying different mechs and difficulties, personally.

As for presentation, the mechs look cool and the music is banging. There's a story of sorts on the campaign which kinda has a comic book or Saturday morning cartoon feel to it, but I'm gonna be honest, the writing is very cringey. Thankfully it is not voiced (none of the game is), it's fairly short and you can just button mash your way through it. It's just random nonsense, so you're not missing much by skipping it.

Besides the story, my only negative is your weapons feel very weak. It's cool to be able to play as a mech for once instead of a ship, but it's unfortunate that despite the multiple weapon combinations, none of them feel like they pack a punch. The bullets are tiny, slow and don't have much of a spread. Everybody knows the coolest part of a shoot em up is starting with a basic pea shooter and powering up to imposing barrages that cover large portions of the screen, there isn't any of that here. You're stuck with the two weapons you pick for your loadout, there's power ups you can pick along the stage that do increase your fire power, but they're time based and go away too fast to be able to get any joy from using them, it would be cool if they at least lasted until you got killed or something. Furthermore, the upgrades you get mid stage and from the shop are mostly stat only stuff, they just make numbers go up or down, there's no visual change to your shots at all, big bummer. I do appreciate that there's a melee option though (actually makes me feel like the mechs aren't just reskinned ships) and that the mechs unique skills are more fun to use than your regular weapons.

Overall, just about good enough for the asking price, but picking it up for cheaper on a sale may make you appreciate it more.

고를 수 있는 기체(5종)와 주무기 및 보조 무기(각각 7종)의 종류가 다양해서 같은 스테이지를 플레이 해도 세팅에 따라서 느낌이 꽤 다른 게임입니다.

 화력에 올인한 기체에 범위가 좁지만 공격력이 뛰어난 주무기와 범위 관통 능력을 갖춘 보조 무기같은 극단적인 공격 지향 조합도 가능하고 방어적인 기체와 넓게 퍼지는 주무기에 목표를 자동으로 쫒아가는 보조 무기로 넓은 범위의 탄막을 유지하는 조합도 가능하고 아군 적군 죄다 총질하는데 혼자 근접전 특화 기체에 사거리 짧은 화염방사기 + 수류탄같은 걸 골라서 고통받는 것도 가능합니다.

 그리고 스테이지를 클리어할 때마다 기본 능력치를 올리거나 패시브 능력을 가진 장비를 구입해서 기체를 강화하는 RPG 요소가 있어서  오래 붙들고 하기에도 괜찮습니다.

 멀티 플레이가 가능하긴 하지만 아쉽게도 온라인 서버를 지원하지 않는 관계로 PC 한 대에 최대 4인까지 로컬 코옵을 즐길 수 있습니다. PC에 조이스틱만 연결하면 그리고 같이 할 사람만 있다면 멀티 플레이도 제법 재미나게 즐길 수 있습니다. 보통 코옵 슈팅 게임에서는 아군의 기체끼리 서로 겹쳐지는 게 가능한데 이 게임은 기체끼리 붙으면 서로 밀어내기 때문에 힘들게 탄막을 피하기보다는 아군 기체 뒤에 숨어 있다가 탄막 쪽으로 아군을 밀어서 방패로 쓰는 전략이 굉장히 유용합니다. 혹시 아군이 죽더라도 버튼 연타하면 바로 부활시킬 수 있으니 안심하고 고기방패로 쓰세요.

 플레이 가능한 게임 모드도 캠페인(몰라도 아무 상관 없는 괴상한 내용의 스토리 모드), 건틀렛(기체 업그레이드 기능 없는 무한 모드), 스트라이크(업그레이드 가능한 무한 모드), 챌린지(이런저런 목표 달성하는 모드)까지 네 종류를 지원하고 모드에 따라서는 제법 세세한 난이도 설정도 가능합니다.

 탄막의 난이도는 낮은 편이고 회피 판정도 후한 편이라 약간 스친 정도로는 기체에 대미지를 입지 않으니 어려운 탄막 슈팅을 기대하는 분께는 추천드리지 않습니다.

 정가 다 주고 사기에는 좀 애매하지만 할인 가격으로 구매하기에는 제법 괜찮은 게임이라고 생각합니다. 가끔 80% 세일도 하고 있으니 전자 오락실 스타일의 횡스크롤 메카 슈팅 게임에 흥미가 있으신 분들은 찜 목록에 넣어 두고 지켜보시면 좋을 것 같네요.

Stardust Galaxy Warriors: Stellar Climax, ou como eu prefiro chamar, apenas de Stardust, é um jogo de ''navinha'' como é conhecido no Brasil, ou shoot 'em up, nome original do gênero. No jogo, ao invés de controlarmos naves, controlamos mechas/robôs gigantes por diversas fases. Tem um level design nas cenários e efeitos gráficos espetaculares. A trilha sonora não fica atrás, possuindo ótimas músicas com batidas de rock e de música eletrônica. Na jogabilidade, podemos jogar da forma tradicional, atirando e se esquivando ou, até fazer com que nossos personagens atirem sozinhos, permitindo nos preocuparmos apenas em se esquivar dos tiros inimigos, sendo muito útil. Existem diversos modos de dificuldade, e de jogo. Contém diversos personagens, armas primárias e secundárias, além de vários power-ups para usar. Possui cooperativo local ou por Remote Play, para até quatro jogadores jogarem simultaneamente.  Conta com uma história de fundo, narrada por diálogos entre os personagens, porém o jogo não conta com nosso idioma. Sendo assim, é difícil de entender tudo perfeitamente. É provavelmente, o melhor jogo do estilo aqui na Steam. Se você é fã de jogos do gênero, esse título é altamente recomendado !

I've had half of an eye on Stardust Galaxy Warriors since it hit Steam Greenlight. I bought it, and my impression of it then was that it was an alright introduction to shmups. I'd hoped to get some of my friends into shmups by playing this with them, but due to my IRL friends being non-gamers, this didn't pan out. I've attempted to get myself through some of the achievements every now and then, so I've put an hour into this game "here and there," and then I put the game down again because I wanted to play something else - I must admit that this game was not made for someone like me. Yet somehow, I keep finding myself playing this game alone, and every time I pick it up I am not disappointed. This game has, so far, been the highlight of my quest through my backlog.

This game is an excellent introduction to this genre of games for a new player - there are recharging shields that make for an incredibly forgiving experience, the bullet density is very rarely too much for a new player to handle on the normal settings, and anything that does an excessive amount of damage is telegraphed very obviously. Never does the game feel like an exercise in memorization, and never does anything feel particularly unfair.

The player is given a very diverse set of tools to handle the challenges that come their way - there's an upgrade system in the campaign that allows players to shore up their weaknesses, powerups are plentiful (and can also be upgraded), and the weapon loadout system allows for a player to choose just about any two shot types they could want. The player also has a sword with which they can quickly hit something in front of them (this is of questionable value). Moreover, there are now five different mechs with different melee abilities and different distortion abilities (think "bomb").

This leads in to the core strength of Stardust Galaxy Warriors: the game is incredibly customizable. The difficulty settings can be tweaked very finely if the player wants, so they can always feel challenged without feeling like the game is unfair. Although this locks the player out of some of the achievements, this is irrelevant: someone who is overly concerned with achievements shouldn't be upset that they can't set everything down to "stupid-easy" and get what they want.

Moreover, the game has local multiplayer, which makes this an incredibly excellent party game. I've pulled this out a few times in this scenario, and I was not disappointed with the results.

I would make the argument that the existence of overpowered loadouts (railgun + torpedo launcher) is kind of worrying, but I wouldn't say it's a dealbreaker for a game with these particular strengths. Other than that, I struggle to find anything seriously negative to say about this game that actually detracts from its strengths.

It is worth pointing out that this is not a game for veterans to play competitively for high scores- I can see someone reasonable giving this game a negative review from that perspective, if they wanted a very competitive game. I don't see steam leaderboards for this game - this is a very good thing, because it doesn't give off the impression that this is a serious game for serious people to get competitive at.

There is something I wish to point out, and this is what spurred me to write a positive review as opposed to just not writing anything at all:

Every time I have played this game, I have noticed that there was a patch or new feature that changed some tiny part of the game. I only play this game every few months, but this would mean that the devs have been constantly improving this game. I have watched this game get custom upgrades, I have watched problematic custom upgrades get removed (triple shot was already a stupidly powerful powerup, and there was an upgrade that let you get triple shot permanently...), I've watched drones become a thing, I've watched the powerups change repeatedly to make them more balanced, and I've watched boss patterns change to become always seemingly fresh. As far as I can tell, a lot of these updates are done quietly, whereas in any other game they'd be met with at least a tiny bit of fanfare.

The top review is a comment on how great the dev team is, over helping someone with a disability play their game. My impression is that this is not even half of the story with respect to how great this dev team is. These devs have worked at this game a lot, and the final product - assuming that this *is* the final product - is incredibly polished.

This is *the* casual shmup to pick up, if you haven't picked up such a game.

Stardust Galaxy Warriors is that type of games where you inevitably end up disappointed, because it's so much fun you never get enough of it. Easily one of the best scrolling shoot'em up/bullet hell of all times.

I reduced all speeds and firing rates to 50% and he can manage just fine (actually he's grown quite proficient at it in just a week of play). I expect we'll still be playing this in ten years, gradually leveling up the difficulty to see how far we can go; and it might just be the perfect couch game when he invites friends over in a few years.

To sum it up: buy and play, and then you can die happily.
